articles.text:

articles.title: Tamil-speaking political parties urge Govt to review Health Assistants’ uniform regulations
articles.text:
The Political Council of Tamil-Speaking Peoples has called on the government to urgently review the existing uniform regulations for Health Assistants, taking into consideration cultural and religious sensitivities while maintaining professional standards and patient safety.
In a letter addressed to the Minister of Health today (17), Opposition MP Shanakiyan Rasamanickam, Convenor of the Political Council of Tamil-Speaking Peoples, urged the government to take necessary steps to address concerns surrounding the regulations.
The letter follows recommendations made by the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka (HRCSL) regarding the issue.
The Council emphasised that uniform regulations should accommodate legitimate cultural, religious and modesty-related preferences while upholding clinical hygiene and professional standards.
It also called on the government to review and amend the relevant circular and establish a clear, practical and inclusive national policy applicable to all public healthcare institutions.
Referring to the Health Minister’s invitation in Parliament to submit proposals, the Council sought clarification on whether the proposed committee had been formally appointed, the progress made so far and the timeframe for issuing a revised national circular.
The Council further stressed that while Opposition political parties are prepared to contribute proposals and support a fair solution, the responsibility for implementing the necessary policy changes rests with the government.
It also urged the Ministry to provide a prompt response and a clear timeline to prevent unnecessary communal tensions over the issue.
The letter was issued on behalf of six political parties, including the All Ceylon Makkal Congress (ACMC), Ceylon Workers’ Congress (CWC), Democratic Tamil National Alliance (DTNA), Ilankai Tamil Arasu Katchi (ITAK), Sri Lanka Muslim Congress (SLMC) and Tamil Progressive Alliance (TPA).
articles.summary: The Political Council of Tamil-Speaking Peoples has called on the government to urgently review the existing uniform regulations for Health Assistants, taking into consideration cultural and religious sensitivities while maintaining professional standards and patient safety.

articles.title: Severe lightning advisory : Red alerts issued for 16 districts
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued a severe lightning advisory for several parts of Sri Lanka, with red alerts issued for 16 districts and amber alerts for nine districts.
According to the advisory, issued at 11.30 a.m. today (17), thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely at several places in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, North-Central, Eastern and Uva provinces, as well as the Mullaitivu District.
The advisory remains in effect until 11.30 p.m. today.
The Met Department warned that temporary, localised strong winds may also occur during thundershowers.
The public has been advised to take necessary precautions to minimise damage caused by lightning, including seeking shelter indoors, avoiding open areas and water bodies, and refraining from using wired telephones and connected electrical appliances during thunderstorms.
People have also been urged to avoid travelling in open vehicles such as bicycles, tractors and boats, and to remain cautious of fallen trees and power lines.
In case of emergencies, the public is advised to contact local disaster management authorities.

The exercise, reported to have taken place on October 17, simulated a road accident involving a lorry transporting radioactive material and a passenger bus.
During the drill, emergency response teams practised safely transporting radiation-contaminated patients from the simulated accident site to the hospital.
The exercise also included decontamination procedures and the provision of emergency medical treatment to affected patients.
The drill was organised to strengthen coordination among emergency response teams and improve preparedness to handle potential radiation-related emergencies.
Doctors, nurses and other hospital staff, along with officers of the Galle Police and members of the Tri-Forces, participated in the exercise.

articles.title: Veteran Indian musician Deva passes away at 75
articles.text:
Veteran Indian Tamil film composer and singer Deva, popularly known as ‘Thenisai Thendral’, passed away in Chennai on Saturday, October 17, according to reports. He was 75.
Reports state that the composer was admitted to Surya Hospital at around 8.30 am, where he died suddenly. Further details regarding the circumstances of his death are awaited.
Born Devanesan Chokkalingam on November 20, 1950, Deva was one of the prominent composers in Tamil cinema, known for his distinctive melodies, folk-based compositions and contributions to the popularity of gaana music in mainstream films. Over a career spanning more than three decades, he composed music for hundreds of films across Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam cinema.
Deva rose to prominence in Tamil cinema in the late 1980s and early 1990s. His collaborations with leading filmmakers and actors resulted in several memorable soundtracks. His notable works include Annamalai, Baashha, Aasai, Kadhal Kottai, Nerrukku Ner, Ninaithen Vandhai, Priyamudan, Vaalee and Kushi. His music played a significant role in shaping the soundtracks of several commercially successful films during the 1990s.
The composer was particularly recognised for bringing the sounds and rhythms of Chennai’s gaana tradition into mainstream Tamil film music. While his energetic, folk-influenced numbers became a signature, Deva also composed romantic melodies and devotional songs, demonstrating his versatility across genres.
His contributions earned him several honours, including the Tamil Nadu government’s Kalaimamani award. He also received the Tamil Nadu State Film Award for Best Music Director for his work in Aasai. Deva’s musical legacy extended to his family. His son, Srikanth Deva, went on to establish himself as a film composer, while his brothers Sabesh and Murali also worked in the film music industry.
Further details regarding his final rites and tributes from members of the film fraternity are awaited. (Cinema Express)
articles.summary: Veteran Indian Tamil film composer and singer Deva, popularly known as ‘Thenisai Thendral’, passed away in Chennai on Saturday, October 17, according to reports. His son, Srikanth Deva, went on to establish himself as a film composer, while his brothers Sabesh and Murali also worked in the film music industry.

articles.title: Over 125kg of smuggled Kendu leaves seized in Puttalam
articles.text:
The Sri Lanka Navy, with the assistance of the Sri Lanka Coast Guard, has seized approximately 125kg of smuggled Kendu leaves during a joint search operation in the Periyapadu coastal area of Puttalam.
According to the Navy, the operation was conducted on Friday morning (16) by personnel attached to SLNS Thambapanni of the Northwestern Naval Command, together with Coast Guard personnel.
During the search, naval personnel inspected three suspicious sacks found along the coast and discovered the stock of Kendu leaves.
The Navy suspects that smugglers may have abandoned the consignment due to increased naval surveillance in the area.
The seized Kendu leaves were handed over to the Puttalam office of the Department of Excise for further legal proceedings.

articles.title: Cricket meets music: SRH owner Kavya Maran set to marry Anirudh Ravichander
articles.text:
In a high-profile union bringing together Indian cricket and the music industry, Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) owner Kavya Maran is set to marry popular Indian music composer and singer Anirudh Ravichander in November 2026.
The wedding plans have effectively been confirmed after Kavya’s parents, Sun Group chairman Kalanithi Maran and his wife Kavery Maran, personally invited Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy to the couple’s wedding reception.
According to Indian media reports, the reception will be held in Chennai on November 21, while the wedding ceremony is reportedly planned for November 11 in Greece. The Greece ceremony has not yet been officially confirmed.
Kavya Maran is one of the most recognisable faces in the Indian Premier League (IPL), regularly appearing at Sunrisers Hyderabad matches and player auctions. She plays a prominent role in managing the franchise, which is owned by her family’s Sun Group.
Anirudh Ravichander, meanwhile, is among India’s leading music composers, having delivered several blockbuster soundtracks for Tamil and Hindi films, including Jailer, Jawan and Leo. He first rose to international fame with the viral song Why This Kolaveri Di.
Speculation surrounding their relationship first attracted widespread attention in 2025, although Anirudh publicly dismissed marriage rumours at the time.
The rumours resurfaced in June 2026 when Anirudh’s uncle, actor Y. G. Mahendran, indicated during an interview that the composer was preparing to marry Kavya.
The latest development follows months of speculation, with the reported invitation to the Telangana chief minister providing the clearest confirmation yet of the couple’s wedding plans.
Neither Anirudh nor Kavya has publicly announced the full wedding arrangements.
articles.summary: In a high-profile union bringing together Indian cricket and the music industry, Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) owner Kavya Maran is set to marry popular Indian music composer and singer Anirudh Ravichander in November 2026. The wedding plans have effectively been confirmed after Kavya’s parents, Sun Group chairman Kalanithi Maran and his wife Kavery Maran, personally invited Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy to the couple’s wedding reception.

articles.title: Rs. 3.09 Bn surgical ward complex planned for Tangalle Hospital
articles.text:
Plans are underway to construct a nine-storey surgical ward complex at the Tangalle Base Hospital at an estimated cost of Rs. 3.09 billion, as part of efforts to expand healthcare services in the Hambantota District.
According to the Ministry of Health, construction is expected to begin by the end of 2026, with the project scheduled to be completed in four phases.
The proposed development was discussed during an inspection visit to the Tangalle Base Hospital by Deputy Minister of Health Hansaka Wijemuni on Wednesday (14).
During a meeting with hospital officials, attention was also focused on constructing a five-storey medical ward complex to address space limitations and improve patient care.
Discussions were also held on providing the hospital with a CT scanner and other modern medical equipment to strengthen diagnostic and treatment services.
The Tangalle Base Hospital, which has a capacity of 339 beds, is one of the main government healthcare institutions serving the Hambantota District.
The Deputy Minister also reviewed staff shortages, ambulance facilities and other essential resources required for the hospital’s daily operations.
Deputy Minister Wijemuni said the development projects would be carried out in coordination with the relevant Provincial Council, with financial support from the Central Government.

articles.title: Govt aims to eradicate poverty within this generation: Minister
articles.text:
The government aims to eradicate poverty within the current generation by empowering low-income communities and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities, Minister of Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment Upali Pannilage said.
Issuing a message to mark the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty, which falls today (17), the Minister said eliminating poverty remains a key priority of the National People’s Power (NPP) government.
He said the government’s approach goes beyond providing financial assistance, focusing instead on strengthening the economic and social capacities of vulnerable communities through self-employment, income-generating opportunities and sustainable livelihoods.
The Minister noted that the government has introduced the ‘Praja Shakthi’ National Programme to eradicate poverty and empower rural communities by identifying their needs and improving living standards.
He said Rs. 25 billion has been allocated for the programme under the 2026 Budget, with plans to implement at least one development project in every Grama Niladhari Division across the country.
Minister Pannilage further emphasised that poverty eradication requires the collective efforts of government institutions, the private sector, civil society organisations and local communities.
He also stressed the importance of addressing the root causes of poverty through long-term solutions while ensuring that no individual or family is left behind in the country’s development process.
The Minister reiterated that the government’s ultimate objective is to build a poverty-free Sri Lanka where social justice is ensured and every citizen has the opportunity to lead a dignified life.
articles.summary: The government aims to eradicate poverty within the current generation by empowering low-income communities and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities, Minister of Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment Upali Pannilage said. The Minister noted that the government has introduced the ‘Praja Shakthi’ National Programme to eradicate poverty and empower rural communities by identifying their needs and improving living standards.

articles.title: Former LTTE member reveals alleged discussions with missing journalist Prageeth Ekneligoda in court
articles.text:
A former LTTE member has testified before a three-judge High Court bench that he maintained a close relationship with missing journalist Prageeth Ekneligoda and had informed senior LTTE figures about their association.
The testimony was given on Friday (October 16) during the trial concerning the abduction and enforced disappearance of Ekneligoda, who went missing in January 2010.
According to court reports, the witness, Sumathipala Suresh Kumar, also known as Murali, told the court that he had maintained a brotherly relationship with Ekneligoda while he was a member of the LTTE.
During cross-examination by defence attorney Asith Siriwardana, Murali said he had shared his wartime experiences with Ekneligoda and had informed senior LTTE figures, including Tamilselvan, Gnanavel and Pottu Amman, about their relationship.
The witness also confirmed that he had previously made a statement concerning a conversation with Ekneligoda at a location in Habarana.
According to his testimony, Ekneligoda had referred to the possibility of changing the country’s leadership by launching a missile at an aircraft carrying then-President Mahinda Rajapaksa.
However, when questioned further by Deputy Solicitor General Wasantha Perera, the witness explained that the comment had been made during a hypothetical discussion about political change following the end of the war.
Murali said he and another individual, identified as Nathan, had been discussing the possibility of living peacefully after the conflict.
He testified that Ekneligoda had responded that although the war had ended, the country’s problems remained unresolved.
When the others suggested that the government could remain in power for another 20 years, Ekneligoda reportedly gave the example of a missile attack on the presidential aircraft to illustrate how quickly political circumstances could change.

According to court reports, the witness, Sumathipala Suresh Kumar, also known as Murali, told the court that he had maintained a brotherly relationship with Ekneligoda while he was a member of the LTTE.

articles.title: Yemen’s government says Houthis fired two missiles at Aden airport
articles.text:
Yemen’s internationally recognised government says the Houthis have launched missiles at the airport in Aden, a day after carrying out a deadly attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city.
Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said two missiles landed near the runway at Aden International Airport on Friday, 500 metres (1,640 feet) from an aircraft that was preparing to take off.
All passengers and crew were safe, he said on X, thanking “divine providence” for preventing a potential “horrific humanitarian catastrophe” and calling the attacks on the airport “a grave violation of international laws and norms”.
The Houthis, in a statement attributed to a military source, said on Friday that they launched an attack on “the Saudi forces’ command headquarters in the Badr camp in Aden province” as well as a weapons depot, the AFP news agency reported.
The latest attack in Aden, which is the seat of the internationally recognised government, comes amid continued heavy fighting in Yemen’s reignited civil war between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-aligned Houthis.
Yemeni government forces said earlier on Friday that troops had advanced in Marib province northeast of Sanaa.
Military spokesman Majed al-Nazili said Yemeni government forces, with air support, had made significant “territorial gains” in the eastern part of the province, securing “key positions”.
He also said Yemeni forces had “neutralised” more than 430 Houthi fighters in 24 hours, while destroying or disabling more than 100 of their vehicles and military assets.
Elsewhere, in Taiz governorate, which has emerged as a key battlefront in the war, Yemeni government forces claimed to have fended off several “large-scale” Houthi attacks, inflicting “heavy losses” on the group.
Yemeni government forces also claimed to have captured a specialised drone team affiliated with the Houthis in the Taiz area.
In recent weeks, Houthi forces have encircled the city of Taiz — Yemen’s third largest urban centre — by ⁠cutting its main road south to Aden, causing widespread ⁠displacement and worsening a humanitarian crisis.
Missiles over Riyadh
Elsewhere on Friday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said it had downed missiles and drones over Riyadh and other parts of Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia has accused Iran of encouraging Houthi attacks against the kingdom, including by arming and training the group.
But Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Friday rejected the accusation, saying Tehran had not played a role in any Houthi operations. The ministry also reiterated a proposal to mediate between the Houthis and Riyadh.
The war in Yemen erupted in 2014 when the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), seized the capital, Sanaa, and forced the government to flee.
An international military coalition led by Saudi Arabia intervened in support of the internationally recognised government in 2015, leading to years of fighting between the warring sides.
A 2022 UN-backed truce halted most fighting, but tensions have been high in Yemen since the Houthis declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabian ports and shipping passing through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait in July.
In September, the Houthis carried out a lightning ground offensive on Mocha, pushing back forces loyal to Yemen’s government from the Red Sea port city.
The same month, the group’s forces again swept through and seized territory along the western coast and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, including the strategically located Mayyun Island in the strait. (Al Jazeera)
articles.summary: Yemen’s internationally recognised government says the Houthis have launched missiles at the airport in Aden, a day after carrying out a deadly attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city. The latest attack in Aden, which is the seat of the internationally recognised government, comes amid continued heavy fighting in Yemen’s reignited civil war between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-aligned Houthis.

articles.title: Historic Nuwara Eliya Post Office undergoes major restoration

According to the Postal Department, the project aims to attract both local and foreign tourists while safeguarding the historic building, which had previously been at the centre of controversy.
Postmaster General Ruwan Sathkumara recently conducted an inspection visit to the Nuwara Eliya Post Office premises to review the progress of the ongoing restoration work.
During the visit, discussions were held with officials from the Sri Lanka Navy, Department of Archaeology and Department of Buildings, who are involved in the conservation project.
The discussions focused on the project’s progress, future development plans and maintaining the quality of restoration work.
Deputy Postmaster General (Central) Aslam Hassan, Deputy Postmaster General (Administration/Development – Acting) Chameesha de Silva, and senior officials from the relevant departments and the Sri Lanka Navy participated in the discussions.
The Postal Department reiterated its commitment to preserving the historic Nuwara Eliya Post Office for future generations while enhancing its contribution to Sri Lanka’s tourism industry.

articles.text:
Police have recovered over 80 grams of cocaine from a female foreign national who was arrested earlier this week in connection with a drug trafficking investigation.
According to Police, the cocaine, weighing 80.9 grams, was recovered from excrement passed by the suspect during a medical examination at the Colombo National Hospital yesterday (16).
The examination was conducted following a court order to determine whether the suspects had concealed cocaine inside their bodies.
The female suspect was among four foreign nationals, including two men and two women, arrested by the Colombo District Crime Division during an operation at a hotel and a shopping mall in Colpetty on October 12.
Police had seized 1.46 kilograms of cocaine during the initial operation.
The four suspects were subsequently produced before the Fort Magistrate’s Court, which granted seven-day detention orders for further questioning.
The Colombo District Crime Division is conducting further investigations.

articles.title: Who shot Kavantissa? Questions remain after iconic tusker’s death
articles.text:
The death of Kavantissa, one of Sri Lanka’s most iconic wild tuskers, has raised fresh questions over who was responsible for the gunshot injury he suffered and whether sufficient action was taken to identify those involved.
Environmentalists are demanding an independent investigation into the elephant’s death, while wildlife authorities prepare to conduct a post-mortem examination to establish the exact cause.
Environmentalist Nayanaka Ranwella has called for an independent examination of Kavantissa’s remains and an investigation to identify whoever was responsible for shooting the animal.
He also raised concerns over the treatment provided to the tusker before his death.
Kavantissa died on Friday (October 16) after battling serious health complications for several weeks. The elephant had been receiving veterinary treatment since September 24 for an injury to his right front leg, reportedly caused by gunfire.
However, questions remain over the circumstances of the shooting, including when and where it occurred and who was responsible.
On October 4, media reports said wildlife veterinarians had confirmed a gunshot injury to Kavantissa’s front leg.
Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi told the media at the time that teams were investigating the shooting. He said wildlife officers had initially noticed changes in the elephant’s movements before reporting the matter to the department’s headquarters.
A newspaper report also highlighted concerns raised by wildlife officers over the availability of firearms among farmers in areas affected by human-elephant conflict.
Wildlife officers also alleged that some local political leaders had interfered with efforts to take action against those responsible for shooting elephants.
These concerns have brought renewed attention to the circumstances in which Kavantissa sustained his injuries.
The shooting first came to public attention in late September. Wildlife enthusiasts reported observing Kavantissa moving normally near Galgamuwa on September 20 before noticing the elephant limping the following day.
A closer inspection revealed an apparent gunshot wound near the right front knee.
Wildlife veterinarians subsequently told the media that the elephant had been sedated so the wound could be cleaned and treated with antibiotics.
However, an earlier report published by Lankadeepa on September 25 quoted the Galgamuwa Wildlife Office as saying veterinarians had not observed evidence of pellets in the elephant’s body. The office also disputed claims circulating on social media about the shooting.
Subsequent reporting, including statements attributed to wildlife veterinarians and officials, identified the injury as a gunshot wound.
Kavantissa initially showed signs of recovery but later developed further health complications.
On October 12, Wildlife Assistant Director Channa Sooriyaweera said the elephant had moved from Galgamuwa towards Thambuttegama, where wildlife officers located him suffering from diarrhoea.
Veterinary teams continued treating both the original injury and his subsequent illness.
On Friday morning, Kavantissa was discovered collapsed in a paddy field in the Siyambalangamuwa area, around two kilometres from the location where he had received treatment the previous day.
Despite efforts by wildlife veterinary teams to save him, the elephant died at approximately 6:18 p.m.
The Department of Wildlife Conservation said it would seek a court order on Saturday (October 17) to conduct a post-mortem examination.
A specialist team, including experts from the University of Peradeniya, is expected to examine the remains to establish the cause of death.
Meanwhile, the demand for an independent investigation has renewed calls for accountability in cases involving injuries to protected wildlife.
Although the Environment Minister previously confirmed that teams were investigating the shooting, no suspect, arrest or conclusive finding identifying the person responsible could be established from the publicly available reports reviewed.
The post-mortem examination may determine what caused Kavantissa’s death, but the separate question of who inflicted the gunshot injury remains unanswered.
articles.summary: The death of Kavantissa, one of Sri Lanka’s most iconic wild tuskers, has raised fresh questions over who was responsible for the gunshot injury he suffered and whether sufficient action was taken to identify those involved. On October 4, media reports said wildlife veterinarians had confirmed a gunshot injury to Kavantissa’s front leg.

articles.title: Rosamund Pike Calls for Landmine Clearance in Sri Lanka After Meeting Survivor
articles.text:
Oscar-nominated British actress and Mines Advisory Group (MAG) Global Ambassador Rosamund Pike has highlighted the critical importance of humanitarian mine clearance in Sri Lanka, sharing the harrowing story of a local landmine survivor to advocate for total clearance of it.
In a personal social media reflection following her visit to Sri Lanka alongside the humanitarian demining organization, Pike detailed her encounter with Victoria, a survivor who suffered life-altering injuries as a teenager after unknowingly interacting with an explosive device while gathering firewood. “During my recent visit to Sri Lanka with Mines Advisory Group, I had the privilege of meeting Victoria,” Pike shared. “When she was 18, she found an interesting object lying on the ground while she was out collecting firewood. She didn’t know what it was but her curiosity got the better of her. She wanted to open it, and find out what might be inside. Her first instinct was to bite it… nothing happened. She threw it on the ground and tried to kick it. Again, nothing happened. She lifted it into her lap and sat down to exert some pressure on what she thought was the lid. She pushed her upper hand firmly into the object to try and release it. And then she woke up in hospital: missing two hands, part of her face and having suffered internal injuries to the area near her heart.” she said.
Describing Victoria’s journey as a “remarkable story of resilience and hope,” the MAG Ambassador underscored the persistent danger posed by landmines remaining in former conflict zones decades after it had ended.
“Her story also shows why this work matters. Landmines and unexploded weapons can remain hidden for decades, putting children at risk as they go about their everyday lives,” Pike emphasized. “The land must be cleared, so that no other child has to face what Victoria did.” she noted.
articles.summary: Oscar-nominated British actress and Mines Advisory Group (MAG) Global Ambassador Rosamund Pike has highlighted the critical importance of humanitarian mine clearance in Sri Lanka, sharing the harrowing story of a local landmine survivor to advocate for total clearance of it.

articles.title: Sri Lanka mourns loss of iconic tusker Kawanthissa
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has lost one of its most iconic wild elephants, Kawanthissa, a majestic tusker whose towering presence and magnificent tusks made him a celebrated figure among wildlife enthusiasts and conservationists.
Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa announced the death of Kawanthissa, who had been receiving veterinary treatment for nearly a month following a gunshot injury.
Believed to be between 50 and 60 years old, Kawanthissa stood approximately 11 feet tall, with tusks measuring more than six feet in length. He was widely regarded as one of Sri Lanka’s tallest living wild tuskers.
First spotted in 2008, the elephant was named Kawanthissa in 2015 after the ancient Sri Lankan ruler King Kawan Tissa, father of King Dutugemunu.
The tusker was a familiar sight in the Galgamuwa, Usgala and Siyambalangamuwa areas of the Kurunegala District, where he roamed for years, becoming a favourite among wildlife photographers and elephant enthusiasts.
Despite his enormous size, Kawanthissa was reportedly not known to have killed or injured anyone.
His final struggle began in September when wildlife observers discovered a gunshot injury near his right front leg. Wildlife veterinarians began treatment on September 24, initially reporting signs of recovery.
However, his condition subsequently deteriorated, with the elephant developing further health complications and losing his appetite.
On October 16, Kawanthissa was found collapsed in a paddy field near Siyambalangamuwa, prompting an emergency operation by wildlife veterinarians. The government also sought assistance from veterinary specialists in Thailand.
His death has renewed concerns over the protection of Sri Lanka’s remaining iconic tuskers, particularly as human-elephant conflict, habitat loss and deliberate shootings continue to threaten the country’s wild elephant population.
For wildlife enthusiasts who followed his movements for nearly two decades, Kawanthissa’s death marks the loss of another irreplaceable symbol of Sri Lanka’s natural heritage.

articles.title: Sri Lanka donates traditional Raksha Masks to FAO Museum in Rome to mark first anniversary
articles.text:
Marking the first anniversary of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) Museum at the FAO headquarters in Rome, the Embassy of Sri Lanka donated three traditional wooden Raksha masks to the museum on October 16, 2026. The initiative was carried out as a gift in support of cultural heritage preservation, in collaboration with the Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau (SLTPB) and the National Craft Council (NCC) of Sri Lanka.
Mask making stands as one of Sri Lanka’s distinctive folk-art traditions rooted in ritual, storytelling and community ceremonies. Passed down through generations, this craft features vibrant colors, intricate carvings and rich symbolism, holding significant value in traditional agrarian rituals where they were believed to protect crops from disease, drought, and pests.
The donated collection features three specific masks crafted by master craftsman R.M.L. Ravindra of Ambalangoda, a second-generation practitioner of the traditional family art. These include the Cobra Demon Mask (Naga Raksha), which represents protection, fertility, wisdom, and guardianship, reflecting the traditional association of snakes with water resources, rainfall and agricultural fertility; the Peacock Demon Mask (Mayura Raksha), which symbolizes beauty, prosperity and good fortune, highlighting the relationship between wildlife, farming landscapes and agricultural biodiversity; and the Fire Demon Mask (Ginidal Raksha), characterized by flame-like carvings, which represents the power of fire to ward off evil and purify, recalling the traditional practice of clearing fields before cultivation and symbolizing renewal and the beginning of a new farming season.
The donation was accompanied by a video message highlighting the importance of preserving cultural heritage. The video featured the Ambassador of Sri Lanka and Permanent Representative to the FAO, Satya Rodrigo; the Head of Outreach and Promotions at the FAO, Clara Velez Fraga; and the Director-General of the International Centre for the Study of the Preservation and Restoration of Cultural Property (ICCROM), Aruna Francesca Maria Gujral.
This contribution reflects Sri Lanka’s longstanding partnership with the FAO and its commitment to sharing its agrarian heritage and cultural traditions with the international community. Through this initiative, the Embassy sought to offer visitors from around the world an insight into the deep connections between nature, ritual, and farming in Sri Lankan life.

articles.title: Clean Serendib Introduces Machine-Assisted Beach Cleaning Technology to Strengthen Coastal Conservation Efforts
articles.text:
Clean Serendib marked the official commencement of its beach-cleaning operations with a demonstration of specialized machine-assisted cleaning technology at Mount Lavinia Beach on 14 October 2026. The initiative introduces a complementary approach to coastal conservation in Sri Lanka, focusing on the removal of smaller waste materials that are often difficult to recover through conventional manual cleaning methods.
The demonstration showcased how mechanized cleaning can enhance existing beach conservation efforts by addressing waste particles embedded within the sand. The event provided invited stakeholders with an opportunity to observe the technology in operation and understand its potential contribution to improving the cleanliness of Sri Lanka’s coastal environments.
Established under the leadership of Founder and Chief Executive Officer Aravinda Athukorala, Clean Serendib is dedicated to advancing practical solutions for coastal cleanliness and environmental preservation. The organization seeks to complement the work of volunteer groups, environmental organizations and public institutions by introducing specialized equipment capable of addressing persistent challenges in beach waste removal.
While conventional beach-cleaning activities play an important role in collecting visible litter, smaller discarded materials, including plastic fragments, bottle caps and other debris, frequently remain embedded beneath the sand. Recovering these materials manually can be labor-intensive, highlighting the value of mechanical cleaning technologies as a complementary solution.
The equipment deployed by Clean Serendib operates through a mechanical screening process designed to separate waste from beach sand. As the machine moves across the beach, it lifts approximately one to two inches of sand and passes the material through an integrated sieve. Sand is returned to the beach while waste particles larger than the sieve openings are separated and retained in an onboard collection compartment for subsequent removal.
Commenting on the initiative, Aravinda, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Clean Serendib, stated:
“Sri Lanka’s beaches are among our most valuable natural assets, and protecting them requires consistent effort and practical solutions. Volunteer groups and environmental organizations already make an invaluable contribution to keeping our coastlines clean. Our objective is to build on those efforts by introducing technology that addresses the smaller waste materials that conventional cleaning methods struggle to remove. We believe machine-assisted cleaning can make a meaningful contribution to coastal conservation, and our ambition is to establish a sustained program that helps preserve these environments for future generations.”

Clean Serendib will also explore opportunities to collaborate with coastal establishments and other stakeholders whose interests align with maintaining clean and accessible beaches, supporting the long-term continuity of its operations.

articles.title: Gnanasara Thera: Govt will not bend the law for any individual, says Minister
articles.text:
Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Nalinda Jayatissa says the government will not bend or amend the law to accommodate any individual, stressing that the law must be applied equally to everyone, regardless of their power or social status.
Responding to questions regarding the ongoing protests by Buddhist monks demanding the release of Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, Minister Jayatissa said the government remains committed to ensuring equal application of the law.
He stated that one of the key reasons behind President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s election victory and the government’s two-thirds parliamentary majority was public dissatisfaction with the unequal application of the law under previous administrations.
According to the Minister, the public had witnessed instances where ordinary citizens were treated differently from those holding political power or enjoying influential positions.
Jayatissa said the government had pledged to end such practices and ensure that the law is enforced equally, irrespective of an individual’s position or status.
He emphasised that this was not only an expectation of those who voted for the government but also of those who did not.
Responding to a question regarding requests for Gnanasara Thera’s release, similar to the presidential pardon granted under the previous Yahapalana government, Jayatissa stressed that the monk’s sentence was imposed by a court.
He noted that individuals have the right to appeal court decisions and that the relevant legal proceedings had already concluded.
The Minister maintained that the government is responsible for implementing court orders and cannot make exceptions based on an individual’s identity or social standing.
He further stated that the public does not expect the government to alter or adjust the law for the benefit of a single individual, adding that all decisions would be made in accordance with established legal procedures.
Meanwhile, Buddhist monks have been staging protests demanding the release of Gnanasara Thera, following a protest march titled “Justice for the Robe – Freedom March,” which commenced from the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic in Kandy on October 10.
The protesters arrived outside the Presidential Secretariat in Colombo on October 15 and remained overnight, demanding a definite response from the government.
However, following a court order prohibiting protests at the location, the monks removed their temporary shelters and subsequently proceeded to the Ministry of Buddhasasana today (16).
The Ministry provided an opportunity for discussions, with four representatives of the protesting monks participating in the meeting.
The members of the Maha Sangha, who engaged in discussions at the Ministry of Buddhasasana, have stated that they would remain at Viharamahadevi Park until Ven. Gnanasara Thero is released. (Newswire)

articles.title: Over 1.6 million driving licence cards and vehicle number plates pending issuance
articles.text:
Sri Lanka is facing a major backlog in the issuance of driving licence cards and vehicle registration number plates, with more than 1.6 million items pending, a Parliamentary committee has been informed.
The issue was raised during a recent meeting of the Ministerial Consultative Committee on Transport, Highways and Urban Development, chaired by Minister Bimal Rathnayake.
Officials revealed that approximately 673,000 driving licence cards remain pending due to shortages of printing equipment and blank cards.
Commissioner General of Motor Traffic, retired Air Vice Marshal Thushara Indunil Fernando, said the existing stock of one million ordered cards is expected to be exhausted by January 2027.
Although a new contract has been awarded for the supply of two million cards, the first shipment is expected only by the end of March 2027.
To address the anticipated shortage, officials are proposing to obtain Cabinet approval to purchase an additional 500,000 cards from the existing supplier.
The commissioner general expressed confidence that the driving licence card backlog could be fully cleared by the middle of 2027.
Meanwhile, the committee was informed that approximately 958,651 vehicle registration number plates remain pending from applications accumulated between Jan. 1, 2025, and March 9, 2026.
The commissioner general said the number plate backlog could be cleared within seven to eight months if the existing contractor is assigned the necessary production work.
Minister Rathnayake instructed officials to take urgent measures to resolve the delays and improve the efficiency of the issuance process.

Officials revealed that approximately 673,000 driving licence cards remain pending due to shortages of printing equipment and blank cards.

articles.title: Driving licences to be suspended at 30 demerit points under new system
articles.text:
Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake says the main objective of Sri Lanka’s new driving licence demerit points system is to penalize motorists who repeatedly violate traffic regulations.
Speaking at a recent Parliamentary Ministerial Consultative Committee meeting, the minister said the system is being introduced through a six-month pilot project, which will continue until March 31, 2027.
Under the proposed system, demerit points will be added to a driver’s record depending on the severity of traffic violations.
Once a driver accumulates 30 points, the system will automatically suspend their driving licence.
Drivers whose licences are suspended will be required to surrender them to the nearest police station.
The suspension will generally last one year, although drivers who successfully complete prescribed training programmes may have the suspension period reduced to three months.
Under the proposed procedure, motorists who commit traffic offences will also receive SMS notifications informing them of the demerit points associated with their violations after paying the relevant fines.
The minister emphasized that the initiative is not intended to intimidate motorists but to encourage compliance with traffic regulations and improve road safety.
The pilot project is designed to familiarize motorists with the system before its full implementation.

Under the proposed system, demerit points will be added to a driver’s record depending on the severity of traffic violations.

articles.text:

articles.title: Sajith visits ailing Tusker Kawanthissa
articles.text:
Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa visited the Siyambalangamuwa area today (16) to inquire into the condition of tusker Kawanthissa, who was found collapsed in a paddy field after suffering from health complications.
During the visit, Premadasa met with veterinary officers treating the tusker and inquired about its current condition and further treatment.
Speaking to the media, the Opposition Leader said Kawanthissa’s condition was one of the consequences of the ongoing human-elephant conflict in Sri Lanka.
He stressed the need for a sustainable solution to the conflict, ensuring that elephants have sufficient forest habitats while allowing people to continue their agricultural activities.
Premadasa also called for a special conservation programme to protect Sri Lanka’s declining tusker population, noting that only a few elephants with large tusks remain in the country.
He proposed establishing a dedicated task force for tusker conservation and implementing a national programme to minimise human-elephant conflict.
The Opposition Leader also commended the efforts of the Department of Wildlife Conservation, veterinary surgeons and volunteers involved in treating Kawanthissa.
Meanwhile, Kawanthissa, considered one of Sri Lanka’s largest and tallest tuskers, was found collapsed in a paddy field in Siyambalangamuwa this morning after reportedly being ill for several days.
The tusker, which inhabits the Getadiulwewa area of Galgamuwa in Mahawa, had previously received treatment for an injury to its right front leg, believed to have been caused by a gunshot.
Treatment for the injury reportedly commenced on September 24, and although the leg injury had healed, the tusker is believed to be suffering from another illness.
Premadasa had previously raised concerns over Kawanthissa’s health in Parliament on several occasions, drawing the attention of the Government and the relevant Minister to the matter.

articles.title: Israeli company used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say
articles.text:
Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads ​that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday.
Its services gave Israel’s Candiru, a spyware company blacklisted by the US government, as ‌well as other Israeli surveillance firms access to advertising platforms run by Google, Comcast, Russia’s Yandex and others, according to separate reports from Canadian cyber watchdog group Citizen Lab and New York advertising security firm Confiant.
The reports show how the online advertising business, long a subject of privacy concerns, can also serve as a channel for sweeping espionage campaigns.
“The way online advertising works today is a systemic security threat,” Wolfie Christl, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab, told Reuters. “For states, the private sector, civil ​society and everyone else alike.”
Discover-Tech’s online ads — often for ordinary products such as phones or earbuds — reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps through its various partnerships, Citizen Lab said.
Users who ​visited sites or used apps with the malicious ads could be identified and tracked by Discover-Tech, which would sometimes also try to extract phone numbers from ⁠some smartphone users, the researchers said. Ads only needed to load on a website for the spying to occur.
Some ads would be used to help plant spyware from Candiru on users’ devices, both research groups ​said, though Confiant said that ads it tied to Candiru were a tiny fraction of Discover-Tech’s overall volume.
MALICIOUS ADS SHOWN IN HUNDREDS OF SENSITIVE NETWORKS
Confiant cofounder Jerome Dangu said Discover-Tech was pumping out at least ​10 million ads per day all around the world and that data-sharing arrangements — called cookie matching — allowed it to track people even beyond the reach of its advertisements.
“Very likely hundreds of millions of people would have been touched by Discover-Tech,” Dangu said.
Discover-Tech, which was founded in 2020, did not return messages left via its contact form. A LinkedIn message and emails sent to its chief executive, Dekel Boni, were not returned.
Reuters’ attempts to reach Candiru’s owners were similarly unsuccessful. The ​US Commerce Department blacklisted Candiru in 2021 for allegedly supplying spyware that was used to maliciously target government officials, journalists, activists and academics.
Citizen Lab said a powerful form of Candiru spyware delivered through Discover-Tech’s ads had ​been used to compromise 45 Windows devices at the Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025, something it said it was able to confirm because the media group had shared its network logs with the group.
In a ‌statement, Al Jazeera ⁠said it “condemns the spyware attacks targeting a number of its staff” and that it was taking steps to protect its employees and its systems. “Those responsible must be held accountable,” it said.
Dangu of Confiant said that the malicious ads had been shown to users in “hundreds of networks in sensitive categories,” including the Pentagon, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court. He also said that some regions, like the Palestinian territories, were particularly saturated by the Israeli firm’s ads.
“You go to almost any site in Palestine — any site — you find a Discover-Tech ad. It gives them a very complete visibility on the digital activities of an ​entire country,” he said.
Citizen Lab also said it ​had similar evidence showing the malicious ads were ⁠shown to people in the United Nations, NATO, the European Commission, and more than a dozen national governments. Other networks the ads appeared in included chip-related firms such as Nvidia, Sandisk, Broadcom, and Micron, as well as several media organizations in Mexico, Israel, and Europe that were not identified.
In addition to identifying ​Candiru and a couple of other surveillance vendors, Citizen Lab said it was able to glean some details about where Discover-Tech’s users might be based ​because the firm inadvertently exposed ⁠its authentication logs to the internet, showing people logging in from internet protocol addresses in Israel, Europe, and the Gulf.
MEASURES AGAINST DISCOVER-TECH TAKEN
Discover-Tech is now being frozen out of parts of the online ad market.
Google said in a statement that it had collaborated with Citizen Lab and Confiant’s investigation and kicked Discover-Tech off its ad platforms “for systematically violating our policies.”
IAB Europe, the European-level association for the digital marketing and advertising ecosystem, said in an email ⁠that Discover-Tech had ​been suspended from its list of globally approved vendors last week after an audit identified policy violations.
Comcast ad tech subsidiary ​Beeswax removed Discover-Tech from its platform “following recent activity,” Comcast said in a statement. Yandex did not return Reuters messages seeking comment.
Advertising-driven surveillance is increasingly being seen as a national security threat. Earlier this year, the Pentagon said it had received reports that US ​forces deployed to war zones had been targeted using location data harvested by ad tech firms and data brokers. Branches of the military have since disabled ad tracking on some devices.
articles.summary: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads ​that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday.

articles.title: SriLankan Airlines extends suspension of Saudi flights until October 24
articles.text:
SriLankan Airlines has announced that the suspension of all flights between Colombo and the Saudi Arabian cities of Riyadh and Dammam has been extended until October 24, 2026, due to the prevailing security situation in the region.
In a statement issued today (16), the national carrier said the decision was taken in consideration of the safety and security of passengers and crew.
The airline stated that services to both destinations will resume once the prevailing conditions have been assessed as suitable for commercial flight operations.
SriLankan Airlines has advised passengers seeking further information to contact its hotline on 1979 (within Sri Lanka) or +94 11 777 1979 (international).
Passengers can also contact the airline via WhatsApp on +94 74 444 1979 (chat only), through their travel agents or by visiting its official website, www.srilankan.com .
The airline expressed appreciation for the understanding and cooperation of passengers affected by the extended suspension.

SriLankan Airlines has advised passengers seeking further information to contact its hotline on 1979 (within Sri Lanka) or +94 11 777 1979 (international).

articles.title: Jailed Imran Khan’s woes compound after Pakistan suspends his provincial government
articles.text:
A state of emergency declared ​in Imran Khan’s main political stronghold is another setback for Pakistan’s jailed former prime minister whose health is worsening, according to his family.
President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday declared the emergency in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province bordering Afghanistan that has seen a sharp rise in militant attacks.
It suspended the local government led by Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, accusing it of failing to tackle militancy, and put an opponent from Zardari’s party in charge.
Khan’s ​party says the move, which strips it of resources from the provincial budget, was a pretext for a political takeover ​of the region and to stop supporters marching on Islamabad.
It challenged the emergency rule at Peshawar High Court ⁠in the provincial capital on Wednesday. “It was ridiculous to equate Imran Khan’s basic human rights with a complex issue such as terrorism,” ​said Zulfi Bukhari, a close aide.
Ahead of the emergency, thousands of Khan’s supporters had rallied in the province intending to march to Islamabad to ​demand his release and medical treatment.
Khan’s three sisters and hundreds of supporters, including party leaders, were arrested ahead of the march.
“You can see clearly that things will become harder for Imran Khan,” said Najam Sethi, a political commentator.
“In the current situation, the PTI lost on both counts. It has not been able ​to extract any concessions for Khan while losing control of its government in KP and surrendering its political leaders to imprisonment.”
The situation ​also worsens the long-running tug-of-war between Khan and the powerful Pakistani military chief Asim Munir, the analyst said.
FORMER CRICKETER
The 74-year-old former cricket star was in ‌power from ⁠2018 to 2022 but sent to jail in 2023 on corruption charges, with visits prohibited for months. He denies the charges.
His family and party have been demanding an urgent medical intervention for loss of vision in one eye, fluctuating blood pressure and the psychological fallout of solitary confinement.
The PTI’s last major protest two years ago ended in deadly clashes, while Khan’s arrest in 2023 sparked nationwide riots.
To avoid a ​repeat, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s government ​last week held talks with ⁠the PTI whose demands included private medical assistance for Khan, prison visits and phone calls with his London-based sons.
The government, in turn, was demanding that the PTI publicly condemn Islamist militancy in the province, ​attend the funeral for security personnel killed in militant attacks, and join hands with the government’s ​counter-terrorism fight, according ⁠to Junior Interior Minister Talal Chaudhry.
“We had given them almost everything they asked for” but the PTI rejected the government demands, he told Reuters.
There have been five such states of emergency in Pakistani provinces since 1975, three of them in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and one each in Punjab and ⁠Balochistan province.
All ​of them were reversed within months either through court or political intervention.
Rights groups and ​analysts have questioned the emergency rule, warning against any crackdown.
“We strongly urge the federal government and the PTI to resume a meaningful political dialogue,” said the Human Rights ​Commission of Pakistan, an independent body.

It suspended the local government led by Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, accusing it of failing to tackle militancy, and put an opponent from Zardari’s party in charge.

articles.title: Test Twenty: Cricket’s fourth format to launch in Sri Lanka
articles.text:
Sri Lanka is set to host the inaugural Test Twenty tournament, a new cricket format that combines boys’ and girls’ matches into a single result, at the Singhalese Sports Club (SSC) in Colombo from Nov. 14 to 29.
Organisers have described Test Twenty as cricket’s fourth format, introducing an 80-over competition featuring both red-ball and white-ball cricket in a single day.
According to a statement issued on Oct. 16, the tournament will bring together 160 young cricketers, aged 13 to 21, from around the world, competing in four continental teams.
Each team will consist of 40 players, including 20 girls and 20 boys, with separate girls’ and boys’ XIs contributing to a combined team score.
Under the new format, each match will feature 80 overs, with the first 40 played in traditional white clothing using a red ball during daylight hours.
The remaining 40 overs will be played in coloured clothing using a white ball under floodlights.
Scores from both halves will be combined to determine the winner, meaning runs scored by the girls’ and boys’ teams will contribute equally to the final result.
A toss will determine which team bats first and whether the girls’ or boys’ match takes place first.
Organisers said thousands of young cricketers from five continents had participated in selection trials over the past 300 days, with the final 160 players expected to be announced through a draft later this month.
The tournament’s advisory board includes former international cricket stars AB de Villiers, Matthew Hayden and Sir Clive Lloyd, while the Global Selection Committee is chaired by Rajkumar Sharma, known for coaching Indian batting star Virat Kohli.
Test Twenty founder Gaurav Bahirvani said Sri Lanka had been selected as the inaugural host because of its strong school cricket culture and enthusiasm for the sport.
“We found the right home for it. Sri Lanka fills a stadium for a ‘schoolboy’ match. No country on earth loves its young cricketers the way this island does,” he said.
Bahirvani also thanked Sri Lanka Cricket and the SSC administration for supporting the initiative.
The tournament will begin with an opening ceremony on Nov. 14, with the final scheduled for Nov. 29 and Nov. 30 reserved as an additional day.
Organisers said all matches would be broadcast live on Sony Sports Network, with international broadcast and streaming arrangements also planned.
Test Twenty was created by Bahirvani and is owned by Parity Sports India Private Limited.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka is set to host the inaugural Test Twenty tournament, a new cricket format that combines boys’ and girls’ matches into a single result, at the Singhalese Sports Club (SSC) in Colombo from Nov. 14 to 29. Organisers have described Test Twenty as cricket’s fourth format, introducing an 80-over competition featuring both red-ball and white-ball cricket in a single day.

articles.title: Derana rejects Deputy Minister’s complaint, says presenter questioned Wimal’s claims
articles.text:
TV Derana has strongly defended its 360 programme presenter Kalindu Karunaratne over allegations raised by Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe’s Office concerning an allegedly AI-generated photograph displayed by former Minister Wimal Weerawansa, maintaining that the presenter had appropriately questioned the claims during the live broadcast.
In a letter dated October 15, Derana TV News director Yuwaraj Athukorala rejected the allegations and said the television channel had committed no wrongdoing requiring a public correction.
The response follows a formal complaint from the Deputy Minister’s Office over a photograph allegedly manipulated using artificial intelligence to portray an individual photographed with Abeysinghe as a Buddhist monk.
Derana pointed out that Karunaratne had directly questioned Weerawansa about the identity of the individual in the photograph during the October 12 programme.
When Weerawansa displayed the image from his mobile phone, the presenter specifically asked whether it was confirmed that the individual shown was a layperson.
Weerawansa responded that it was confirmed and later identified the individual as Amal Salinda.
Derana maintained that the presenter had fulfilled his journalistic responsibility by directly questioning the guest about the photograph rather than simply accepting the claim without challenge.
The channel said guests appearing on live television programmes were responsible for the statements they made and the photographs or documents they presented.
It argued that presenters and production teams could not scientifically verify the authenticity of every photograph or document presented during a live broadcast, adding that questioning the guest about the material was the action available to the presenter.
Derana also confirmed that it had not rebroadcast Weerawansa’s remarks on television or republished them on digital platforms following the live programme.
The channel rejected the Deputy Minister’s demand for a correction, maintaining that neither the presenter nor the television station had acted improperly.
However, Derana said it was willing to inform viewers during the next edition of 360 that it had received a letter from the Deputy Minister’s Office alleging that the photograph was AI-generated.
The controversy began after Abeysinghe alleged that a photograph originally showing him alongside an individual identified as Amal, who had helped protect protesters during the 2022 Aragalaya movement, had been digitally manipulated to depict the individual wearing Buddhist robes.
The Deputy Minister subsequently issued a clarification on social media, sharing what he described as the original photograph alongside the allegedly AI-manipulated version.
He accused Weerawansa of using the image to make misleading political claims during the television discussion.
However, the Deputy Minister’s Office confirmed that no letter of demand had been sent to former Minister Wimal Weerawansa, who displayed the photograph and made the remarks.
In its response, Derana questioned why criticism had been directed at the programme presenter over statements and material presented by a guest, expressing surprise at the attempt to hold the presenter responsible.
Derana reiterated that Karunaratne had questioned Weerawansa about the photograph during the live broadcast and maintained that the responsibility for the image and the claims made about it rested with the former Minister Wimal Weerawansa (Newswire).
articles.summary: TV Derana has strongly defended its 360 programme presenter Kalindu Karunaratne over allegations raised by Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe’s Office concerning an allegedly AI-generated photograph displayed by former Minister Wimal Weerawansa, maintaining that the presenter had appropriately questioned the claims during the live broadcast.

articles.title: Ceylan Worldwide: Sri Lanka’s Largest Promotional Apparel Enterprise with Triple ISO Certification
articles.text:
Ceylan Worldwide (Pvt) Ltd has achieved Triple ISO Certification , comprising ISO 9001 (Quality Management), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management), and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety). This milestone positions Ceylan as Sri Lanka’s largest promotional apparel enterprise to hold all three certifications, underscoring its leadership in responsible excellence.
Founded in 2009, Ceylan Worldwide has grown from a pioneering Sri Lankan enterprise into a trusted international partner in premium corporate apparel and customized promotional merchandise. Over the years, the company has built a reputation for excellence, serving a customer base of more than 1,000 organizations worldwide . Guided by innovation, ethical practices, and customercentric values, its operations span marketing, manufacturing, branding execution, and distribution — all supported by a robust Integrated Management System (IMS) Policy.
As a participant of the United Nations Global Compact, Ceylan aligns its strategies with universal principles relating to human rights, labor, environment, and anticorruption. The Triple ISO Certification further reinforces this commitment, ensuring that every product and process contributes positively to people and the community.
Krishan Kollure, Director, said: “Our Triple ISO Certification is a reflection of the discipline and precision in our production processes. From raw material sourcing to final delivery, every stage is managed with strict quality controls, environmental responsibility, and safety standards. This achievement proves that our factory operations are aligned with international benchmarks, ensuring reliability and consistency across every customer order and delivering products that meet our quality standards.”
Sonali Hewage, Director – Corporate Communications & Compliance, said: “Leading this certification journey was both a responsibility and a privilege. Achieving ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and ISO 45001 is a proud achievement that reflects our team’s dedication to quality, sustainability, and workplace safety. With over 15 years of experience, these certifications reinforce the strength of our IMS Policy and our commitment to ensuring product quality, reducing environmental impact, and safeguarding both staff and clients.”
articles.summary: Ceylan Worldwide (Pvt) Ltd has achieved Triple ISO Certification , comprising ISO 9001 (Quality Management), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management), and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety). This milestone positions Ceylan as Sri Lanka’s largest promotional apparel enterprise to hold all three certifications, underscoring its leadership in responsible excellence.
